The synthesis included almost a hundred steps, and involved the characteristic rigorous planning and analyses that had always characterised Woodward's work. Following a grant of land from Emperor [Henry VI](/wiki/Henry_VI,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Henry VI, Holy Roman Emperor") in 1191, Monaco was refounded in 1215 as a colony of Genoa.[[27]](#cite_note-state1-30)[[28]](#cite_note-31) Monaco was first ruled by a member of the House of Grimaldi in 1297, when [Francesco Grimaldi](/wiki/Fran%C3%A7ois_Grimaldi "François Grimaldi"), known as "*Malizia*" (translated from Italian either as "The Malicious One" or "The Cunning One"), and his men captured the fortress protecting the [Rock of Monaco](/wiki/Rock_of_Monaco "Rock of Monaco") while dressed as [Franciscan](/wiki/Franciscans "Franciscans") [friars](/wiki/Friar "Friar") – a *monaco* in Italian – although this is a coincidence as the area was already known by this name.[[29]](#cite_note-32)

Francesco was evicted a few years later by the Genoese forces, and the struggle over "the Rock" continued for another century.[[30]](#cite_note-33) The Grimaldi family was Genoese and the struggle was something of a family feud.
